bug_semantics: GitPython's unsafe-option guards reconstructed candidate options from kwarg names but did not inspect a single-character kwarg's value. With the normal split_single_char_options=True transformation, a call such as clone_from(..., n="--upload-pack=<attacker command>") passes validation as candidate '-n' and is then emitted as two argv tokens, '-n' and '--upload-pack=<attacker command>'; Git interprets the second token and runs the supplied upload-pack command. The shared candidate builder exposed the same value-smuggling primitive through guarded clone/clone_from, fetch, pull, push, ls_remote, revision/iter_commits, blame, and archive paths unless allow_unsafe_options was explicitly enabled.
flaw_origin: Commit 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 introduced the shared _option_candidates guard and its guarded call sites. Its loop derived candidates solely from each kwarg key (for a one-character key, '-<key>') while the already-existing transform_kwarg code emitted a non-boolean one-character kwarg value as a separate argv token. That incomplete security remediation created the guard/value semantic mismatch; the later merge af027be78693962c233cc989915f40e9b135f3a5 is only a carrier, not the BIC.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object header is exactly 'author GPT 5.6 <codex@openai.com> 1783861602 +0200'; it has human committer 'Sebastian Thiel <sebastian.thiel@icloud.com>' and a 'Reviewed-by: Sebastian Thiel <sebastian.thiel@icloud.com>' trailer, with no Co-authored-by or Generated-with trailer. The explicit GPT/Codex author identity is the BIC-only AI signal.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-r9mr-m37c-5fr3 identifies <=3.1.53 as affected and >=3.1.54 as patched, documents _option_candidates([], {'n':'--upload-pack=...'}) -> ['-n'], transform_kwargs -> ['-n','--upload-pack=...'], and the end-to-end command-execution path. In the validated clone, `git log --all --reverse -S'def _option_candidates' -- git/cmd.py` and `git log --all --reverse -S'options.append(f"-{key}" if len(key) == 1 else f"--{dashify(key)}")' -- git/cmd.py` both identify 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 as the first writer; `git log -L 1044,1068:git/cmd.py` shows the key-only function added by 701ce32f, value checking added by e8d0fbf, and a later distinct joined-short-option hardening. `git show 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 -- git/cmd.py git/objects/commit.py git/remote.py git/repo/base.py` displays the new shared builder and guarded consumers. `git rev-parse 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738^` gives 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8; `git grep -n _option_candidates 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 -- git/cmd.py` has no match, while `git show 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8:git/cmd.py` shows the pre-existing split transform, directly proving the flawed guard is absent in the parent. `git cat-file commit 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738` proves the single parent and exact GPT 5.6/Codex author header. `git tag --contains 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738` starts at 3.1.51 (the exact bypassing guard therefore lands in 3.1.51; older versions lacked this guard and remain within the advisory's broader <=3.1.53 affected range). `git show e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453 -- git/cmd.py test/test_git.py` shows the direct fix: for split one-character kwargs it adds dash-prefixed values to the unsafe-option candidate list and regression-checks n='--upload-pack=helper'. Its parent is faf3c09038b03bc2bdd8545ef34bbf6d7f1cd11f, exactly `git rev-list -n 1 3.1.53`; `git tag --contains e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453` starts at 3.1.54, and `git log --reverse 3.1.53..3.1.54` shows e8d0fbf as the first direct fix member before merge a4dc70d4eec15825aac2dfd7484c961f6fc8491b and release commit e59d9bab02b095a97e179f47019afee95f4e3c18.
reasoning: The expected one-character kwarg splitting predates the security control and is not by itself the guard-bypass root cause. The smallest causal change is 701ce32f: it simultaneously introduced the protection contract and the key-only reconstruction that omitted a value which becomes an independent Git option token. The direct parent has no _option_candidates guard, and the merge/release commits merely carry this atomic one-parent change. e8d0fbf directly closes this exact split-value path by validating the emitted option-like value and is included first in 3.1.54. Because the BIC commit object explicitly names GPT 5.6/Codex as author, AI wrote the causal defective guard itself, so the proper closed verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than AI_CODE_FLAWED or NOT_AI.
